RQ2: Do gains in correctness justify energy-greedy architectures?

Santiago del Rey

Load and preprocess data

We load the data from the parquet file, filter out the inception_v3 architecture and the Desktop Normal User training environment, and normalize the energy consumption by the total number of images seen during training (converting MJ to J). We also prepare the gpu_usage variable.

df <- read_parquet("data/metrics/processed/clean-dl-training-energy-consumption-dataset.gzip") %>%
    rename(training_environment = `training environment`, gpu_usage = `gpu usage (%)`, f1_score = `f1-score`, energy = `energy (MJ)`) %>%
    filter(architecture != "inception_v3" & training_environment != "Desktop Normal User") %>%
    mutate(
        energy_per_image = (energy * 1000000) / `total seen images`, # Convert MJ to J and normalize by total seen images
        architecture = case_match(
            architecture,
            "mobilenet_v2" ~ "Mobilenet V2",
            "nasnet_mobile" ~ "NASNet Mobile",
            "resnet50" ~ "ResNet50",
            "xception" ~ "Xception",
            "vgg16" ~ "VGG16"
        ),
        architecture = factor(architecture, levels = c("Mobilenet V2", "NASNet Mobile", "ResNet50", "Xception", "VGG16")),
        # Each architecture has a single GFLOPs value, so this factor is equivalent to the architecture
        GFLOPs = factor(GFLOPs),
        training_environment = factor(training_environment, levels = c("Desktop ML Engineer", "Server")),
        # Relative energy per relative F1-score (lower is more efficient)
        efficiency = (energy / max(energy, na.rm = TRUE)) / (f1_score / max(f1_score, na.rm = TRUE)),
    ) %>%
    dplyr::select(energy, energy_per_image, f1_score, efficiency, GFLOPs, architecture, training_environment, `training duration (h)`)

Outlier filtering functions

# Define a function to filter outliers of a given variable on an input data frame
filter_outliers <- function(df, variable) {
    df %>%
        group_by(GFLOPs, training_environment) %>%
        mutate(
            Q1 = quantile(!!sym(variable), 0.25),
            Q3 = quantile(!!sym(variable), 0.75),
            IQR = Q3 - Q1,
            is_outlier = !!sym(variable) < (Q1 - 1.5 * IQR) | !!sym(variable) > (Q3 + 1.5 * IQR)
        ) %>%
        ungroup() %>%
        filter(!is_outlier) %>%
        dplyr::select(-Q1, -Q3, -IQR, -is_outlier)
}

Data overview

# Filter F1-score outliers
df_clean <- df %>%
    group_by(GFLOPs) %>%
    mutate(
        Q1 = quantile(f1_score, 0.25),
        Q3 = quantile(f1_score, 0.75),
        IQR = Q3 - Q1,
        is_outlier = f1_score < (Q1 - 1.5 * IQR) | f1_score > (Q3 + 1.5 * IQR)
    ) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    dplyr::select(-Q1, -Q3, -IQR)

df_clean %>%
    filter(is_outlier)
df_clean <- df_clean %>%
    filter(!is_outlier) %>%
    dplyr::select(-is_outlier)

nrows <- nrow(df_clean)
df_clean <- filter_outliers(df_clean, "energy_per_image")
print(paste("Number of outliers removed from energy_per_image:", nrows - nrow(df_clean)))
## [1] "Number of outliers removed from energy_per_image: 21"
df_clean %>%
    filter(f1_score < 0.5)
# Display the first few rows of the data frame
head(df_clean)

Model 1: F1-score as a function of GFLOPs

model1 <- lm(f1_logit ~ GFLOPs, data = df_clean)

Model 1 with beta regression

# Transform F1 to (0,1) if any 0s or 1s (Smithson & Verkuilen, using the total sample size)
df_clean <- df_clean %>%
    mutate(f1_trans = (f1_score * (n() - 1) + 0.5) / n())

# Original model
model1_beta <- betareg(f1_trans ~ GFLOPs, data = df_clean)
summary(model1_beta)
## 
## Call:
## betareg(formula = f1_trans ~ GFLOPs, data = df_clean)
## 
## Quantile residuals:
##     Min      1Q  Median      3Q     Max 
## -6.0772  0.1301  0.1960  0.2820  2.2597 
## 
## Coefficients (mean model with logit link):
##                    Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)    
## (Intercept)          2.9262     0.1142  25.623  < 2e-16 ***
## GFLOPs0.37164736     0.1378     0.1589   0.867  0.38585    
## GFLOPs2.52438272    -0.8678     0.1385  -6.268 3.66e-10 ***
## GFLOPs2.958404032    0.3437     0.1566   2.195  0.02816 *  
## GFLOPs10.028770304   0.4487     0.1607   2.792  0.00523 ** 
## 
## Phi coefficients (precision model with identity link):
##       Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)    
## (phi)    22.18       2.10   10.56   <2e-16 ***
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1 
## 
## Type of estimator: ML (maximum likelihood)
## Log-likelihood: 544.6 on 6 Df
## Pseudo R-squared: 0.5242
## Number of iterations: 25 (BFGS) + 2 (Fisher scoring)
# Check residuals
par(mfrow = c(2, 2))
plot(model1_beta)

resid_quant <- residuals(model1_beta, type = "quantile") # Quantile residuals
leverage <- hatvalues(model1_beta) # Influence measures

# Cook's distance analogue (optional, not always directly provided)
# If not available: approximate influence = leverage * (residual^2)
influence_metric <- leverage * (resid_quant^2)

# Combine into a data frame
diagnostics_df <- df_clean %>%
    mutate(
        residuals = resid_quant,
        leverage = leverage,
        influence = influence_metric,
        obs_id = row_number()
    )

# Heuristics
high_leverage <- diagnostics_df$leverage > (2 * mean(diagnostics_df$leverage))
high_residuals <- abs(diagnostics_df$residuals) > 2
high_influence <- diagnostics_df$influence > (2 * mean(diagnostics_df$influence))

# Label flags
diagnostics_df <- diagnostics_df %>%
    mutate(flag = case_when(
        high_leverage & high_residuals ~ "High leverage & residual",
        high_influence ~ "High influence",
        TRUE ~ "Normal"
    ))


ggplot(diagnostics_df, aes(x = leverage, y = residuals, color = flag)) +
    geom_point() +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
    labs(title = "Residuals vs Leverage", x = "Leverage", y = "Quantile Residuals")

ggplot(diagnostics_df, aes(x = obs_id, y = influence)) +
    geom_bar(stat = "identity", fill = "steelblue") +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 2 * mean(diagnostics_df$influence), color = "red", linetype = "dashed") +
    labs(title = "Influence Metric (Cook's Distance Approx.)", x = "Observation", y = "Influence")

diagnostics_df %>%
    arrange(desc(influence)) %>%
    dplyr::select(obs_id, GFLOPs, training_environment, residuals, leverage, influence, flag) %>%
    head(10)
ggplot(filter(diagnostics_df, architecture == "ResNet50"), aes(x = obs_id, y = residuals)) +
    geom_point() +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
    labs(title = "Residuals for ResNet50")

# Post hoc tests for beta regression model
post_hoc_model1_beta <- emmeans(model1_beta, ~GFLOPs, type = "response")
post_hoc_results_model1_beta <- summary(post_hoc_model1_beta)
post_hoc_results_model1_beta
# Plot post hoc results for beta regression model
post_hoc_plot_model1_beta <- ggplot(post_hoc_results_model1_beta, aes(x = GFLOPs, y = emmean)) +
    geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = position_dodge()) +
    # geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lower.CL, ymax = upper.CL), width = 0.2, position = position_dodge(0.9)) +
    labs(title = "Post Hoc Results for Model 1 (Beta Regression)", x = "GFLOPs", y = "Estimated Marginal Mean (F1-score)") +
    theme_minimal() +
    scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set1")
print(post_hoc_plot_model1_beta)

pairs(post_hoc_model1_beta, adjust = "tukey") # Post hoc pairwise comparisons for beta regression model

Model 1 using a GAMLSS

# Full model
full_model <- gamlss(
    f1_score ~ GFLOPs,
    sigma.formula = ~GFLOPs,
    family = BE,
    control = gamlss.control(n.cyc = 100),
    data = df_clean
)

Comparison of the full model (GFLOPs in mu and sigma) against the null model.

lrt_full_vs_null <- deviance(null_model) - deviance(full_model)
df_full_vs_null <- full_model$df.fit - null_model$df.fit
data.frame(
    model = c("null", "full"),
    df = c(null_model$df.fit, full_model$df.fit),
    AIC = c(AIC(null_model), AIC(full_model)),
    delta_AIC = c(AIC(null_model), AIC(full_model)) - AIC(full_model)
)
cat(sprintf("LRT chi2(%d) = %.2f, p = %.3g\n", df_full_vs_null, lrt_full_vs_null, pchisq(lrt_full_vs_null, df_full_vs_null, lower.tail = FALSE)))
## LRT chi2(8) = 1030.64, p = 3.63e-217

Effect of the training environment. The environment-only model tests its marginal effect; adding it to the full model tests its effect given GFLOPs.

model_env_only <- gamlss(f1_score ~ training_environment, sigma.formula = ~1, family = BE, data = df_clean)
## GAMLSS-RS iteration 1: Global Deviance = -906.5191 
## GAMLSS-RS iteration 2: Global Deviance = -968.2189 
## GAMLSS-RS iteration 3: Global Deviance = -1004.294 
## GAMLSS-RS iteration 4: Global Deviance = -1019.425 
## GAMLSS-RS iteration 5: Global Deviance = -1023.879 
## GAMLSS-RS iteration 6: Global Deviance = -1024.873 
## GAMLSS-RS iteration 7: Global Deviance = -1025.061 
## GAMLSS-RS iteration 8: Global Deviance = -1025.094 
## GAMLSS-RS iteration 9: Global Deviance = -1025.099 
## GAMLSS-RS iteration 10: Global Deviance = -1025.1
drop1(model_env_only)
full_model_env <- gamlss(
    f1_score ~ GFLOPs + training_environment,
    sigma.formula = ~GFLOPs,
    family = BE,
    control = gamlss.control(n.cyc = 100),
    data = df_clean
)
## GAMLSS-RS iteration 1: Global Deviance = -939.971 
## GAMLSS-RS iteration 2: Global Deviance = -1057.27 
## GAMLSS-RS iteration 3: Global Deviance = -1209.375 
## GAMLSS-RS iteration 4: Global Deviance = -1422.624 
## GAMLSS-RS iteration 5: Global Deviance = -1740.556 
## GAMLSS-RS iteration 6: Global Deviance = -2031.17 
## GAMLSS-RS iteration 7: Global Deviance = -2083.543 
## GAMLSS-RS iteration 8: Global Deviance = -2084.314 
## GAMLSS-RS iteration 9: Global Deviance = -2084.351 
## GAMLSS-RS iteration 10: Global Deviance = -2084.354 
## GAMLSS-RS iteration 11: Global Deviance = -2084.354
lrt_env <- deviance(full_model) - deviance(full_model_env)
cat(sprintf(
    "Environment given GFLOPs: LRT chi2(1) = %.2f, p = %.3g, delta AIC = %.2f\n",
    lrt_env, pchisq(lrt_env, 1, lower.tail = FALSE), AIC(full_model_env) - AIC(full_model)
))
## Environment given GFLOPs: LRT chi2(1) = 29.70, p = 5.05e-08, delta AIC = -27.70
# Get unique combinations of factors
# Extract predicted means and SE on response scale (mu)
emm <- emmeans(full_model, ~GFLOPs,
    type = "response",
    at = list(sigma = mean(predict(full_model, what = "sigma", type = "response")))
)

# Convert emmeans to dataframe for ggplot
emm_df <- as.data.frame(emm)
emm_df
ggplot(emm_df, aes(x = GFLOPs, y = response)) +
    geom_point(size = 3) +
    geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = asymp.LCL, ymax = asymp.UCL), width = 0.2) +
    ylab("Estimated mean F1 score") +
    xlab("GFLOPs") +
    ggtitle("Effect of Model GFLOPs on F1 Score") +
    theme_minimal()

pairs_emm <- pairs(emm, adjust = "tukey")
pairs_df <- as.data.frame(pairs_emm)
pairs_df
ggplot(pairs_df, aes(x = contrast, y = odds.ratio)) +
    geom_point() +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", color = "red") +
    coord_flip() +
    ylab("Odds Ratio (F1 score)") +
    xlab("GFLOPs contrasts") +
    ggtitle("Pairwise Comparisons of GFLOPs (Tukey adjusted)") +
    theme_minimal()

Model 2: relative energy per relative F1-score as a function of GFLOPs and training environment

model2 <- lm(
    efficiency ~ GFLOPs * training_environment,
    data = df_clean, contrasts = list(GFLOPs = "contr.sum", training_environment = "contr.sum")
)
summary(model2)

Significance of interaction effects

Anova(model2, type = 3)

Post hoc tests for Model 2
